aboutGame.title: What is Gladio Mori?
paragraphs: Gladio Mori is a physics-driven multiplayer gladiator fighting game developed by Plebeian Studio. Step into brutal arenas featuring a cutting-edge organ-based damage system where every slash, thrust, and blunt impact targets physical anatomy rather than a traditional health bar.

Craft your own attack moves using the comprehensive in-game animation move editor, equip 34 authentic weapons and modular armor sets, and engage in tactical arena battles across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S with up to four-player cross-platform PvP.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about Gladio Mori.

items.question: What is Gladio Mori?
items.answer: Gladio Mori is a physics-driven gladiator fighting game featuring realistic organ-based damage rather than conventional health bars. Developed by Plebeian Studio, Gladio Mori lets up to 4 players duel in brutal arenas using 34 weapons, customizable movesets, and full cross-play across PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S.

items.question: How does combat and damage work in Gladio Mori?
items.answer: Combat in Gladio Mori is governed by true physics and anatomical hitboxes. Strikes wound specific body parts, sever arteries, cause internal bleeding, or pierce organs like the heart and brain, causing instantaneous collapse or rapid exhaustion.

items.question: Can you create custom moves in Gladio Mori?
items.answer: Yes, Gladio Mori features an advanced in-game Move Editor that allows players to animate their own attacks, fine-tune keyframes, string fluid combos, and share custom movesets with the community.

items.question: Does Gladio Mori support multiplayer and cross-play?
items.answer: Yes, Gladio Mori supports up to 4-player battles including online PvP, local split-screen couch multiplayer, and full cross-platform play between PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S.

items.question: What weapons and armor are available in Gladio Mori?
items.answer: Gladio Mori features 34 distinct weapons (including longswords, katanas, gladii, polearms, and daggers) and 17 armor pieces. Combatants balance protection and agility using an equipment point system.
